notes:
Summary: Enterprise procurement; large analytics platform for real-time credit scoring and query reranking. Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with hard throughput and latency guarantees, EU data residency for subset of workloads.

Key technical requirements (shorthand):
- Workloads: low-latency chat (p95 < 80ms), reranking pipeline (p95 < 120ms), embeddings batch 400 qps
- Throughput target: sustain 350-450 req/s steady for 99% of windows; burstable to 700 req/s for short periods
- Reserved GPU planning: want 8 x A100-equivalent reserved for baseline, autoscale pool for bursts; estimate 2:1 model replica ratio for redundancy
- Latency SLOs: propose p95 < 80ms for chat, p99 < 200ms for critical endpoints; customer pushing for p95 < 60ms on canary routes

SLA negotiation highlights (from 2026-03-10 meeting):
- Uptime: customer requesting 99.99% for production route (they run credit decisioning). Redwood standard draft: 99.95% for Dedicated with credits.
- Credit schedule discussed: tiered crediting. Redwood proposes: < 99.95% to 99.5% = 10% monthly credit; 99.5% to 98% = 30% credit; <98% = 50% credit. Customer counters: wants steeper credits starting at <99.9%.
- Maintenance windows: Redwood proposes weekly 30-min maintenance window with advance notice; customer asks for quarterly scheduled full-stack windows only and no maintenance during US/EU trading hours (08:00-18:00 local). Need appendix for maintenance blackout windows per region.
- Support response times: Redwood standard P1 1hr, P2 4hr, P3 24hr. Customer wants P1 <=30min and dedicated escalation path to on-call lead during incidents.
- SLA exclusions: capacity throttling due to customer-configured rate limits, DDoS, force majeure to be explicit. Customer legal asked to limit exclusions.

Procurement/legal concerns:
- Liability cap: Redwood standard = 12 months fees. Customer wants 24 months and carve-outs for gross negligence.
- Data residency & audit: Require EU-only routing for EU tenant; annual SOC2 Type II report and right to audit clause.
- Term & termination: customer wants 90-day termination for convenience after year 1; Redwood prefers annual commitment with 60-day notice.

POC / Metrics observed so far:
- Week 1 baseline (small model): sustained 420 req/s with median latency 62ms, p95 98ms (chat), KV-cache reduced tokens 22% on avg.
- Tail optimizations planned: kernel selection tune and batching profile to hit p95 targets under load.

Quotes & paraphrases: "We need ironclad uptime for scoring during market open — any outage is revenue at risk." — Head of Platform (Maplebridge).

Next steps (tactical):
- Jordan to coordinate legal touchpoint; receive redlines by 2026-03-17.
- Priya to produce reserved GPU sizing worksheet (final) and cost delta for higher uptime tiers by 2026-03-14.
- SE to run targeted latency tuning PoC for p95 < 70ms (canary route) during week of 2026-03-15.
- Prepare maintenance blackout appendix and per-region windows for legal review.

Notes style: fragments, bullets, and action items. Follow-ups: track INF-2345 for escalations.
sla_negotiation_summary: Negotiation centerpieces: uptime percent (target 99.99 desired by customer vs Redwood standard 99.95), credit schedule (customer wants earlier/steeper credits), maintenance blackout windows (customer requires trading-hour protection), and support response times (customer requests P1 30m). Legal is focused on liability cap and data residency. Proposal: offer an uplifted SLA package (SLA+): 99.99% uptime for production routes with additional monthly fee (approx +25-40% cost), accelerated credits, and 24/7 priority support with 30-min P1. Need legal signoff and final pricing approval.
